about: No / Yes is the blank two-row version of the Drake format: on the left, Drake in an orange puffer jacket against a yellow wall first turns away with his hand raised in disgust, then points and smiles with approval in the row below. The empty white space to the right of each pose holds the two options. Rejection on top, endorsement below, so the meme states a preference in a single glance, and the comedy usually comes from choosing the worse, lazier or more ridiculous option with full confidence.
origin: Both poses come from the music video for Drake's 2015 single "Hotline Bling". Stills from the video were used as reaction images on 4chan and other forums before the two-panel preference layout became one of the most widely used templates online.
usage:
Put the option being rejected in the top box, next to Drake's grimace, and the preferred option in the bottom box, next to his approving point. Both boxes sit in the white panels on the right side, so short phrases are easier to read than long sentences.

The strongest versions pick a ridiculous winner: the hacky workaround over the real fix, the 40-minute video essay over the 2-minute summary, the nap over the deadline. Keeping the two options parallel in wording makes the reversal sharper.
ideas: watching one more video at 2 am
